subject.title: [Feature]: cron jobs.d/ directory support (one file per job, for NixOS/GitOps declarative setups)

question: Should OpenClaw core add a jobs.d/declarative cron file surface, or should this remain an external ClawHub/plugin or CLI sync workflow on top of the SQLite cron store?
rationale: Current code and policy make SQLite the cron runtime store and set a high bar for new config/file storage surfaces, while this request needs user-facing GitOps semantics that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Keep as product design item
options.body: Keep this issue open until a maintainer chooses the core-vs-plugin direction and the required compatibility/security contract.

options.title: Route to ClawHub/plugin sync
options.body: Close or redirect this if maintainers decide a jobs.d-to-SQLite sync package is sufficient with existing cron APIs.

options.title: Sponsor core declarative sync
options.body: Approve a core design that documents import/sync semantics, preserves SQLite runtime state, and covers doctor, docs, config, and focused cron tests.

recommendation.title: Keep as product design item
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open until a maintainer chooses the core-vs-plugin direction and the required compatibility/security contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent cron SQLite migration and storage refactor history makes steipete the clearest routing candidate for the storage/product boundary decision.
